# India Insignia {background-image="https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/India_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg/1920px-India_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail" background-size="30%" background-position="85% 50%"}

## The National Insignia {background-image="https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/Emblem_of_India.svg/960px-Emblem_of_India.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail" background-size="25%" background-position="95% 50%"}

> National Emblem


::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="70%"}

- Lion Capital of Ashoka, Sarnath (MP).

- Adopted as the state emblem of India: 26 Jan 1950, the day when India became a Republic.

- *Satyameva Jayate* from *Mundaka Upanishad*. It is national motto.

:::

::: {.column}

:::

:::

::: aside
Insignia = चिह्न अधिचिह्न
:::

## The Ashoka Pillar {background-image="https://culturalsamvaad.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Conjectural-View-of-Sarnath-Lion-Capital-e1685285953823-668x1024.jpg" background-size="contain" background-position="right"}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="68%"}

- Capital means top of a pillar, around 7 feet tall on a 50-40 feet tall pillar, at Sarnath.

- Sarnath (MP) where the Buddha gave his first sermon.

- Ashoka, an emperor of Maurya Empire placed pillars like this one at several Buddhist monasteries.

::: 

::: 

::: {.footer}
Information from [UC Berkeley](https://orias.berkeley.edu/lion-capital-ashoka) & image from [Cultural Samvad](https://culturalsamvaad.com/sarnath-lion-capital-from-an-ashokan-pillar-to-indias-state-emblem/)
:::

## The Capital {background-image="https://orias.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/general/day1-1-sarnath_capital_with_numbers.jpg?itok=2t7brxs4&timestamp=1682567623" background-size="contain" background-position="right" .scrollable} 

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="70%" .r-fit-text}

1. The entire piece was the capital. 

1. Horizontal disk is called abacus, it sits between the capital and the pillar.

1. Dharmachakra (Wheel of Law), in Buddhism dharma means the universal law that governs the universe.

1. Four lions on the capital, four cardinal direction, also Buddha, also Ashoka.

1. The abacus has 4 wheels on it, also representing the dharmachakra. 

1. In between the wheels are four animals: an elephant, a bull, a horse, and a lion. These animals were all associated with Buddhism.

1. The bottom of the capital is a lotus.


::: 

::: 

::: {.footer}
Information and image from [UC Berkeley](https://orias.berkeley.edu/lion-capital-ashoka)
:::

## National Anthem

> "Jana Gana Mana"


::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

- Author & Composer: Rabindranath Tagore

- Year Composed: 1911

- Official Adoption Date: January 24, 1950

:::

::: {.column .r-fit-text}

जनगणमन-अधिनायक जय हे भारतभाग्यविधाता!

पंजाब सिंध गुजरात मराठा द्राविड़ उत्कल बंग

विंध्य हिमाचल यमुना गंगा उच्छलजलधितरंग

तव शुभ नामे जागे, तव शुभ आशिष मागेे,

गाहे तव जयगाथा।

जनगणमंगलदायक जय हे भारतभाग्यविधाता!

जय हे, जय हे, जय हे, जय जय जय जय हे॥

:::

:::


## National Song

> "Vande Mataram"


::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

- Author & Composer: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee

- Year Published: 1882

- Official Adoption Date: January 24, 1950

:::

::: {.column .r-fit-text}

वन्दे मातरम्।

सुजलाम् सुफलाम् मलय़जशीतलाम्,

शस्यश्यामलाम् मातरम्। वन्दे मातरम्।

शुभ्रज्योत्स्ना पुलकितयामिनीम्,

फुल्लकुसुमित द्रुमदलशोभिनीम्,

सुहासिनीम् सुमधुरभाषिणीम्,

सुखदाम् वरदाम् मातरम्। वन्दे मातरम्।

:::

:::

## The National Flag 🇮🇳 (The Tricolor)


::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

- Saffron (Kesari): representing courage and sacrifice.

- White: peace and truth.

- Green: faith and chivalry

- Chakra of navy blue

:::

::: {.column}

- Design adopted on 22 July 1947

- Flag Code of India 2002 regulates flat's use and display.

- Prevention of Improper Use Act, 1950 & the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971

:::

:::

## National River

> River Ganga (Ganges)

- The longest in India, flowing over 2,510 kms.

- Source of Ganga is *Gaumukh* in *Gangotri* Himalayan glacier.

- the Bhagirathi, the Alaknanda, the Mandakini, the Dhauliganga, and the Pindar form Ganga

## National Flower

> Lotus

- Scientific Name:	Nelumbo Nucifera Gaertn

- Significance:	Purity, beauty, and spirituality

- Cultural Importance:	Sacred in Indian religions like Hinduism and Buddhism

- Habitat:	Grows in wetlands, ponds, and lakes

## National Tree 

> Indian Banyan Tree


::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="70%"}

- Scientific name: *Ficus Bengalensis*

- It has branches that shoots aerial roots letting it spread like new trees over a large area.

- This tree is considered immortal due to the characteristic of spreading the whole area with its roots, expanding trunk and its longevity.

:::

::: {.column width="30%"}

![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Big_Banyan_Tree_at_Bangalore.jpg/1280px-Big_Banyan_Tree_at_Bangalore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail)

:::

:::

## National Animal

> Royal Bengal Tiger

::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

- Scientific name: Panthera tigris tigris

- In 2022, Bengal tiger population was around 3,167-3,682 in India.

- 'Project Tiger' was launched in April 1973.

## National Currency

<br>

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="70%"}

- The symbol is a combination of both Devanagiri letter 'Ra' and Roman letter 'R' with a stripe cutting at the middle to represent the tricolor.

- The use of Shiro Rekha in Devanagri script is unique to India where letters hangs from the top.

- The sign designed by D. Udaya Kumar, IIT Guwahati, Assam

:::

::: {.column width="30%"}

![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Indian_Rupee_symbol.svg/960px-Indian_Rupee_symbol.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail)

:::

:::

::: footer
Image source: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_rupee_sign#/media/File:Indian_Rupee_symbol.svg)
:::

## National Monument

> India Gate

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="70%"}

- The war memorial, erected in memory of 90,000 soldiers who lost their lives fighting in the World War I and Afghan War for the British Army.

- Designed by **Sir Edwin Lutyens**.

- Earlier name was All India War Memorial.

:::

::: {.column width="30%"}

![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Edwin_Lutyens.jpg/960px-Edwin_Lutyens.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail)

:::

:::

## National Calendar

- At the time of independence, the Government of India followed the Gregorian calender based upon the Christian era.

## Indian Standard Time (IST)

> +5.5 hours of GMT


::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

- India has only one standard time.

- Location of Mirzapur (near Allahabad) and the 82°30'E longitude that is used as the reference longitude for IST

:::

::: {.column width="40%"}

![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/IST-Mirzapur.svg/960px-IST-Mirzapur.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail)

:::
